rationale:
The subject `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.outline_source.fn` only declares the signature `Sources::parse(&self, path: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Result<OutlineContent, SourceError>`. It states no behavior of its own. Behavior belongs to sibling requirements such as `outline_source.behavior` and `provider_results.parse_snapshot`, and they are not assessed here.

The marked tests exercise the signature through the compiler and through assertions on the result:
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/source_defaults.rs#fn[empty_sources_errors_and_retained_snapshots_remain_distinct]` calls `sources.parse(&file("note.txt")).await.unwrap()`. It asserts on the returned `OutlineContent`: `id().path`, `id().selector`, and `text()` staying the same after the file changes.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/source_defaults.rs#fn[built_in_languages_and_structural_search_use_the_project_scope]` calls `parse` on `note.unknown` and `visible.rs`. It asserts on `fingerprint_scheme()` and `outline().items.len()`.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[source_discovery_and_its_pages_do_not_register_reads]` runs the `outline_source` tool through the session. That tool outlines one file snapshot.

These calls cover the async method, the `Path`-like argument, and the `Result<OutlineContent, _>` shape. A wrong signature would fail to compile. The assertions on the returned value check that the content is an outline snapshot. I found no further obligation in the text that needs a test.
